_what: C-9 D2 / gate G3: modular gear in the 3D cliffside. Five stacks on the G key.

axe_at_the_strike.verdict: the blade mass is FORWARD of the haft -- the edge arrives first

axe_caveat: Nothing in the export marks the sharp edge, so this measures the HEAD's mass distribution about the haft along the direction of travel, not the edge itself. A named empty or a vertex group on the blade would make it exact. An earlier pass answered 'the poll arrives first' because its head cluster was defined as vertices past 0.6x reach, which on a 0.851 m axe put the boundary at 0.51 m and measured half the haft.
binding: Every piece -- including the two the manifest calls `socket` -- is exported as a SKINNED mesh on a skeleton whose 24 bone names match the body's, in the same order. So all six bind the same way: reparented under the body's own Skeleton3D, skin kept, `skeleton` pointed at it. A socketed axe would have needed a BoneAttachment3D and a hand-fitted offset, and an offset fitted by eye is a number nobody can check. Where the manifest's mode and the file's content disagree, the file wins; both are recorded per piece.
bracers_note: The manifest lists ten bracer objects. Two are the pair (6258 and 5724 triangles); the other eight are 1-7 triangle slivers totalling 17. Bound anyway, per the manifest; harmless, and worth knowing before 'ten pieces' is reported as working.

poke_through.verdict: NONE VISIBLE at the play camera on the worst frame of each clip -- see GEAR_poke_worst_frames.jpg.
poke_through.why_no_number: Two numerical instruments were built and neither is reportable, which is the honest answer rather than a number I have shown to be wrong. (1) Screen-space -- body pixels drawn in front of a garment inside its silhouette -- reported 4.0-7.3%, and saving the worst frames showed what it had counted: his own forearm and shield crossing his chest. A body part in front of a garment is not poke-through, and no screen test can tell the two apart. (2) Geometric -- the torso unrolled about its spine into height x angle cells, furthest body vertex against nearest garment vertex -- reported 133-294 mm over renders that are clean, and got WORSE with 15x denser sampling, so it is structurally wrong rather than starved: a crude cell cannot represent a shoulder or an armpit, where body and shell are at radii no single cell comparison can match. A correct test needs a nearest-surface query with the garment's own normals, which is not a thing to bolt on at the end of a session.

shield_caveat: GEOMETRIC: shield vertices inside a capsule of radius 0.250 m about the spine, which turns with him. A screen test reported 21-37% 'torso through the shield' and what it had found was a forearm; a world-axis AABB reported 198 of 407 vertices inside a box the torso rattles around in. The capsule number is real and the pictures agree: see GEAR_shield_worst_frames.jpg, where the run frame shows the shield passing through his side.
